Build a LightTAR-style recipe for numeric embeddings

Source: R/make-lighttar-recipe.R
make_lighttar_recipe.Rd

Replace embedding columns with PCA features and a separate block of regularized partial least squares (PLS) features. Both blocks start from the same standardized embeddings. Only PLS uses the outcome. All projections are estimated by recipes::prep() on its training rows and applied by recipes::bake() without the outcome. Other columns are preserved.

Usage

make_lighttar_recipe(
  .data,
  .outcome_var,
  .emb_cols,
  .u_pca = 30L,
  .s_pls = 5L,
  .m = 60
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame containing embeddings, an outcome, and any other predictors. Supply precomputed numeric embeddings; no encoder is run.

.outcome_var

Name of one numeric or factor outcome column.

.emb_cols

Nonempty character vector of unique numeric embedding column names, excluding the outcome.

.u_pca

Positive integer: maximum number of PCA components.

.s_pls

Non-negative integer: maximum number of supervised components. Set to 0 for PCA only.

.m

Non-negative input-variance weight. The fitted PLS penalty is .m / n, where n is the number of training rows. Use 0 for plain PLS.

Value

An untrained recipes::recipe() that creates pca_ and, where applicable, pls_ predictors.

Details

This single-embedding-block version of LightTAR uses the same columns for PCA and PLS. Constant embedding columns contribute no variation; at least one column must vary. The number of components may be smaller than requested if training data are rank deficient or the supervised deflation has no signal left. The PCA and PLS blocks are not jointly orthogonal; choose .u_pca below the embedding rank if you want to leave room for additional signal. Embeddings and training outcomes must be finite and complete (factors must have no missing values).

References

Shapira et al., LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning, https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17600.

Examples

rec <- make_lighttar_recipe(mtcars, "mpg", c("disp", "hp", "wt"), 2, 1)
trained <- recipes::prep(rec, training = mtcars[1:24, ])
recipes::bake(trained, new_data = mtcars[25:32, ])
